correctness.rationale: For edge lengths a>=b and acute δ, projected widths Aθ=a|sinθ|,Bθ=b|sin(θ-δ)|, and area C=ab sinδ. Conditional width-weighted Crofton orientation and trapezoidal transverse chord profile yield the exact survival integral over angles. Cavalieri gives μ=πC/[2(a+b)]. For x<=h=b sinδ all directions remain active, and evaluating ∫|sinθ sin(θ-δ)|dθ=J(δ) gives κ=J(δ)/[(a+b)sinδ]. The first exclusion occurs at transverse maximum A=a, with a positive local plateau a-b cosδ; one or two maximizers create the claimed sqrt(u) cusp. The inverse α=a/(a+b), q=J(δ) is unique because J strictly decreases from π/2 to 1. At δ=π/2, J(π/2-ε)=1+ε²/2+O(ε^4), giving sharp Hölder exponent 1/2. Independent analytic/numerical invariant checks were executed on square, rectangle, rhombus, oblique cases. The proof, not quadrature, covers all shapes.
residual_risks: The ideal exact law-level cutoff is sensitive to finite sampling; no estimator or stability bound for noisy h is established.

final_claim: For invariant-motion-measure isotropic line chords of a nondegenerate Euclidean parallelogram, the mean chord μ, initial survival slope κ, and first nonaffine cutoff h determine the congruence class; feasible α=2μ/(πh) in [1/2,1), q=κh/(1-α) in [1,π/2), with a sharp square-root cusp at h and square-root inverse-angle singularity at rectangles.
limitations: Only exact invariant-line chord law for nondegenerate Euclidean parallelograms; no estimator under sampling noise and no other quadrilateral classes.
